label: Well-Adjusted Male Graduate
summary: This profile represents respondents who report notably low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. With UCLA-8 loneliness scores, PHQ-9 depression scores, and GAD-7 anxiety scores all well below typical thresholds, these individuals appear to be psychologically well-adjusted. They engage in moderate daily screen or internet use (1-3 hours) and hold graduate-level or higher education.
demographic_anchor: Male, graduate-level education or above, 1-3 hours of daily internet/screen use
behavior_markers: Very low loneliness levels (UCLA-8 mean: 0.79, indicating minimal social isolation)
Near-floor depressive symptom scores (PHQ-9 mean: 0.28, suggesting negligible depression)
Extremely low anxiety symptom scores (GAD-7 mean: 0.04, indicating virtually no anxiety)
Moderate and controlled internet/screen usage of 1-3 hours daily
Higher educational attainment suggesting structured daily routines and cognitive engagement

label: Digitally Over-Immersed & Emotionally Distressed
summary: This profile captures highly educated women who spend more than five hours daily on digital devices and report elevated levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety. Their loneliness scores (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 1.66) sit above typical thresholds, while depressive symptoms (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 1.65) and especially anxiety symptoms (GAD-7 mean ≈ 2.10) are notably high, suggesting a co-occurring pattern of psychological distress. With 198 respondents in this cluster, the profile represents a sizable subgroup characterized by the convergence of heavy screen time and multi-dimensional emotional vulnerability.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, daily screen time exceeding 5 hours
behavior_markers: Reports higher-than-average loneliness on the UCLA-8 scale
Endorses elevated depressive symptoms on the PHQ-9
Scores highest among profiles on GAD-7 anxiety items
Engages in prolonged daily screen use (more than 5 hours)
Co-occurrence of loneliness, depression, and anxiety suggests compounding emotional distress
tone: Concerned and empathetic, reflecting the convergence of multiple psychological stressors in a high-education, high-screen-time demographic

label: Resilient Well-Connected Graduate Woman
summary: This profile represents respondents who report consistently low levels of loneliness, depressive symptoms, and anxiety symptoms. Across all three validated scales (UCLA-8, PHQ-9, GAD-7), mean scores fall well below clinical thresholds, indicating generally positive mental health and strong social connectedness. The profile comprises 309 respondents in the training split, making it a substantial and reliable cluster.
demographic_anchor: Female, graduate-level education or above, 1–3 hours of daily screen/social-media use
behavior_markers: Reports minimal loneliness (UCLA-8 mean ≈ 1.21, near the scale floor)
Exhibits very low depressive symptomatology (PHQ-9 mean ≈ 0.82, well below mild-depression cutoff)
Displays very low anxiety symptomatology (GAD-7 mean ≈ 0.79, well below mild-anxiety cutoff)
Maintains moderate and bounded screen or social-media use (1–3 hours daily)
Holds advanced educational attainment, suggesting access to cognitive and social resources
tone: Calm, emotionally stable, and socially engaged
